title: Severity of Powered Personal Transporter (E-Scooter) Casualties in Great Britain, 2021-2025: A Comparative Analysis with Pedal Cyclists and Motorcyclists Using STATS19 Data
description:
Analysis of five years (2021-2025) of UK STATS19 police-reported collision data comparing injury severity between e-scooter, pedal cycle, and motorcycle casualties. Severity is measured as killed or seriously injured (KASI).

Key findings:

  • E-scooter casualty counts were stable across the period (1,102 in 2021 to 1,162 in 2025), but the KASI proportion rose from 0.284 (95% CI 0.258-0.311) to 0.358 (0.331-0.386).
  • E-scooter casualties were younger than pedal cyclists (median age 22 vs 35) and predominantly urban (94.0% vs 84.0%).
  • After adjustment for age, sex, speed limit, lighting, road type, urban/rural classification and junction detail, e-scooter casualties had 1.59 times the odds of KASI compared with pedal cyclists (95% CI 1.49-1.69).
  • The estimate was robust to correction for the concurrent change to injury-based severity reporting: 1.56 (1.47-1.66) using the DfT severity adjustment, and 1.64 (1.50-1.78) restricted to injury-based-reporting forces.

Important limitation: no exposure denominator exists for this mode, so these are severity proportions among casualties, not estimates of risk per trip or per kilometre.

Includes the full analysis code, which reproduces the derived dataset byte-identically from the raw data. Raw data is not redistributed; it is retrieved from the Department for Transport by the included script.
notes: Data source: STATS19 road safety open data, UK Department for Transport, Open Government Licence v3.0, Crown copyright. This is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.
